business_summary.text: Diamond Power Infrastructure manufactures power transmission and distribution cables and conductors, from low voltage to extra-high voltage, at an integrated complex in Vadodara, Gujarat.

call_points.text: Order book ₹3,688 Cr as on 11 Aug 2026, about 2x last year's revenue.
Adani is ~40% of order book; board mandate to cut to 20% by year-end.
Two aluminium corrugation lines approved for ₹17 Cr, converting 33 kV capacity to 66/132 kV.
Sixth CCV line to be ordered this month, commissioned by December 2027.
LV cable brownfield facility to add ~42,000 km capacity, ~₹1,880 Cr revenue potential, commercial production FY28.
QIP of ₹1,614 Cr turned net worth from negative ₹922 Cr to positive ₹691 Cr.
QIP use: ₹130 Cr LV expansion, ₹74 Cr balancing equipment, ₹325 Cr general corporate, ₹350 Cr promoter loan repayment, ~₹750 Cr working capital.
Only debt left is ₹1,900 Cr 0.01% promoter-held bonds payable after 30 years, NPV ₹47 Cr.
Operating cost cut from 9% to 6.5%, internal target 6%.
Monsoon flooding hit Q1; management says without it revenue would have been ₹70-80 Cr higher.
Export order book target of at least ₹500 Cr this year, first export year.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: An Appeal has been preferred against the Order passed for FY 2017-18 by the State Tax Officer before the Hon’ble Deputy Commissioner (Appeals) of State Tax, Vadodara against the confirmation of demand of Rs. 41,43,244/- plus interest of Rs. 41,43,244/- and a penalty of Rs. 4,14,324/- for confirmation of demand on the alleged difference of ITC availed when compared to GSTR-9, Ineligible ITC availment under Section 17(5), 16(4) and from dealers who have filed NIL Returns. The Honourable National Company Law Tribunal, Ahmedabad vide IA/160(AHM)2022 in CP(IB) 137 of 2018 while sanctioning the resolution plan of M/s. GSEC Ltd. for Corporate Debtor held as under: “As far as reliefs and concessions claimed by the resolution applicant, the law has been well settled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ghanashyam Mishra and Sons Private Limited Vs. Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company Limited and Ors. reported in MANU/SC/0273/2021 in the following words: (i)“The legislative intent behind this is, to freeze all the claims so that the resolution applicant starts on a clean slate and is not flung with any surprise claims. If that is permitted, the very calculations on the basis of which the resolution applicant submits its plans, would go haywire and the plan would be unworkable. (ii)We have no hesitation to say, that the word "other stakeholders" would squarely cover the Central Government, any State Government or any local authorities. The legislature, noticing that on account of obvious omission, certain tax authorities were not abiding by the mandate of I&B Code and continuing with the proceedings, has brought out the 2019 amendment so as to cure the said mischief… 17. In view of the above, all past claims would stand extinguished. However, as far as various statutory rights vested with the Corporate Debtor in form of various licenses, leases, and others alike matter, we make it clear that the successful resolution applicant has to approach the concerned statutory authority for those concessions and those authorities will consider the same as per their established procedure.” Thus, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Section 238 thereof stipulating that provisions of aforesaid Code have overriding effect on any other law for time being in force - Non obstante clause in Section 238 ibid and word ‘shall’ used in Section 31(1) ibid makes it abundantly clear that a resolution plan approved by committee of creditors and further approved by National Company Law Tribunal would be binding on all creditors including Central Government, any State Government or any local authority to whom a debt in respect of payment of dues arising under any law for time being in force. Accordingly, no liability though exists on the part of the company, the demand has been created in Electronic Liability Register and hence the same has been shown as contingent liability.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: State Tax Officer, Ghatak-40, Range-10, Division-5, Vadodara
tax_litigation.status: The same is pending before the Hon’ble Deputy Commissioner (Appeals) of State Tax, Vadodara. No Change in Status during the quarter ended 31.12.2025

operating_notes.text: Company discharged in PMLA Case No. 2/2024 by Special Court, Ahmedabad on May 6, 2026.
No proceedings are now pending against the company under PMLA.
PMLA Special Court discharge lifts embargo on fixed assets of ₹1,000+ Cr and receivables of ₹900+ Cr, plus assets of subsidiary Diamond Power Transformers Limited.
Company says its manufacturing capacities are presently highly under-utilised and it plans balancing equipment, debottlenecking and modernisation.
Commissioned 7th MV/EHV cable line at Vadodara facility, adding 150 kms/month capacity for ₹55 crore.
Commissioned 7th MV/EHV cable line at Vadodara facility using CCV technology.
MPS non-compliance for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 is still continuing; BSE and NSE fined ₹4,50,000 each (₹5,31,000 with GST), paid on 20 May 2026.
FY26 capex was ₹81.22 Cr against ₹67.67 Cr in FY25, with CWIP of ₹152.32 Cr at 31 March 2026.
Unsecured inter-company deposits rose ₹230.64 Cr in FY26 to fund the business as borrowings fell ₹59.78 Cr.
Auditor's opinion is qualified on both consolidated and standalone results over physical verification and valuation of Property, Plant & Equipment.
Commissioned 8th MV/EHV power cable line at Vadodara with 150 kms/month capacity for ₹30 Cr via internal accruals.
Commissioned 8th MV/EHV power cable line at Vadodara; two more lines under installation, expected operational on or before 31 March 2027, taking the facility to 10 lines.
Order book ₹3,688 Cr as on 11 August 2026, with ₹845 Cr to be executed in the next year and ₹2,800 Cr to be delivered before March 2027.
Adani is around 40% of the order book; the board mandate is to bring it to 20% by year-end.
Data centre order book ₹435 Cr; target of ₹1,000 Cr of data centre orders before 31 March 2027.
Existing capacity includes 6 CCV lines (~2,000 km p.a. EHV capacity) running at 60% utilisation.

timeline.summary: Diamond Power Infrastructure was discharged by the Special PMLA Court in Ahmedabad in PMLA Case No. 2/2024, concluding all pending PMLA proceedings against the company.
2026-05-08: Special PMLA Court, Ahmedabad discharged Diamond Power in PMLA Case No. 2/2024 by order of 6 May 2026, lifting the embargo on fixed assets of ₹1,000+ Cr and receivables of ₹900+ Cr.
Diamond Power Infrastructure commissioned its 7th MV/EHV cable line at Vadodara, adding 150 kms/month capacity for ₹55 crore.
Diamond Power Infrastructure successfully commissioned its 7th MV/EHV cable line based on CCV technology at its Vadodara facility.
GSEC Limited’s **Rakesh Ramanlal Shah** (MD) declared on **April 1, 2026**, no encumbrances by **Rakesh Shah** and **Shaishav Rakesh Shah** beyond prior disclosures for FY2025-26.
Diamond Power incurred ₹5.31 lakh in penalties from BSE and NSE for Minimum Public Shareholding non-compliance.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹695.87 Cr (+108.5% YoY), net profit ₹60.61 Cr (+691.3% YoY).
Diamond Power Infrastructure reported FY26 revenue of ₹1,910.10 Cr with a net profit of ₹158.17 Cr.
Diamond Power Infrastructure commissioned its 8th MV/EHV power cable production line at Vadodara, adding 150 kms/month capacity for ₹30 Cr.
On June 3, 2026, Diamond Power announced the commissioning of its 8th MV/EHV power cable production line at Vadodara.
On October 19, 2026, Diamond Power Infrastructure appointed Kundip S. Thakker as CFO effective October 20, 2026.
Diamond Power announced a ₹25 Cr internal-accrual capex to add a CCV line for cables up to 132 kV by December 2027.
